review.scope: Synthesis of existing ledger episodes and the first faction-consistency pass. No fresh news intake was performed for the interface redesign.

administration.headline: Midterm defeat forces a fight over personnel, policy and accountability.
administration.summary: Republicans’ midterm rout has turned personnel changes into a fight over the direction of Trump’s second term. The announced replacement of Wiles with Miller points toward stronger hardliner agenda access, not yet a verified policy reversal. Incoming Democratic majorities will gain subpoena, hearing and funding leverage when the next Congress convenes. The likely near-term contest is over accountability and war costs: Democrats can raise the cost of continuity, while Trump can reshuffle personnel and shift blame without changing course. Watch military orders, enforcement changes and budget concessions to distinguish a policy reset from a change of messengers.

contests.title: White House access is shifting
contests.assessment: Miller’s announced promotion promises broader access for the Maximalists. Wiles’s move changes the Operation’s White House role; it does not establish a transfer of campaign-money control.
contests.authority: Trump appoints the chief of staff. The reported handover is November 9.
contests.leverage: Miller gains a prospective agenda channel; Wiles retains a reported political-operation role.
contests.change: Appointment announced; exercised authority still pending.

basis.actions: Trump named Miller to succeed Wiles.
basis.positions: Public congratulations preserve unity; they establish no 2028 endorsement.
basis.money: No financial cause for the appointment is established. Campaign resources and White House access are separate channels.

contests.watch: Confirm the handover and each adviser’s actual remit.
contests.summary: Miller is positioned to gain agenda access. Wiles’s political remit and the November 9 handover remain to be verified.

contests.title: Iran policy remains a contested decision
contests.assessment: Vance has a negotiating channel and a public case for ending the war. Rubio’s defense of Trump supplies a rival position. Neither establishes control over Trump’s next military decision or a completed settlement.
contests.authority: Trump directs military decisions; Congress controls appropriations and has war powers.
contests.leverage: Negotiators influence the options. Public criticism changes political positioning before it changes policy.
contests.change: A visible split over the war’s political costs; the policy outcome remains open.

basis.actions: Trump reviewed options; Vance has led negotiations.
basis.positions: Vance publicly blamed the war for electoral losses; Rubio defended Trump’s decision.
basis.money: Deal-Capital’s business exposure is relevant context, not proof of donor direction of negotiations.

contests.watch: Look for an order, observable operational change or an accepted agreement.
contests.summary: Vance’s negotiating role competes with hawkish arguments; Trump retains the military decision.

contests.title: The succession coalition is still open
contests.assessment: Vance has the clearest recorded organizational route. Rubio retains a competing institutional and donor lane. Trump has not settled the succession question in the reviewed record.
contests.authority: Republican voters and the nomination process decide the nominee. Trump’s support is an influential endorsement channel.
contests.leverage: Party fundraising, organizations, donor access and public positioning supply distinct forms of leverage.
contests.change: Vance’s post-election argument separates him from hawkish rivals without demonstrating a gain in voter support.

basis.actions: The RNC finance role, Malik fundraiser and Turning Point backing are concrete channels.
basis.positions: Public deferral, message support and a candidate endorsement mean different things.
basis.money: Thiel’s historical backing and Rockbridge access help explain Vance’s network; Griffin’s reported preference is not a Rubio contribution pledge.

contests.watch: Track entry intentions, endorsements, organizing and new support evidence.
contests.summary: Vance has the clearest organizational route. Rubio retains a competing donor and institutional lane.

contests.title: Fed governance has institutional limits
contests.assessment: White House pressure on Cook remains constrained by legal process. Treasury’s policy influence must be distinguished from the FOMC’s authority over rates.
contests.authority: The FOMC votes on rates. Removal disputes involve the presidency and courts under the applicable law.
contests.leverage: Advisers can shape pressure and process; that does not give a faction control over the rate vote.
contests.change: Cook’s hearing schedule and process remain unresolved in the reviewed coverage.

basis.actions: The hearing was delayed; the later filing addressed scheduling and participation.
basis.positions: Calls for lower rates do not establish a changed vote or removal.
basis.money: Market exposure can explain interests; no payment causing a rate decision is established.

contests.watch: Verify the hearing notice, court disposition and any action actually taken.
contests.summary: White House pressure is constrained by legal process. Rate authority remains with the FOMC.

nomination.headline: Vance leads; the coalition is not settled.
nomination.summary: Vance has the strongest recorded organizational route. Rubio is a credible competing lane; DeSantis, Cruz and McEntee rely on progressively more conditional coalition-building assumptions. The exact weights remain provisional judgments.

candidates.path: The best-established route to inherit Trump’s coalition.
candidates.coalition: RNC fundraising, Rockbridge and Turning Point channels.
candidates.vulnerability: Administration ownership and a contested restraint record.
candidates.positions: Economic nationalism, immigration restriction and a negotiating role.
candidates.money: Historical Thiel backing; access does not imply agreement on every policy.

candidates.path: An institutional alternative with an overlapping hawkish donor lane.
candidates.coalition: State/NSC relationships and donors who prefer him.
candidates.advantage: National visibility and an existing policy network.
candidates.vulnerability: Whether he enters, and responsibility for a war he defended.
candidates.positions: Hawkish commitments coexist with deference to Trump.
candidates.money: Griffin preference and prospective donor interest are not pledged 2028 funds.

candidates.path: A state-executive alternative if federal incumbents lose credibility.
candidates.coalition: Social conservatives and voters seeking distance from Washington.
candidates.advantage: Executive experience outside the federal decision chain.
candidates.vulnerability: Coalition rebuilding is assumed more than demonstrated.
candidates.positions: Enacted state policies; support for limited strikes complicates a restraint pitch.
candidates.money: Past fundraising capacity is not a verified current donor coalition.

candidates.path: A hawkish, tariff-skeptical alternative to Vance.
candidates.coalition: Religious conservatives and overlapping hawkish networks.
candidates.advantage: A recognizable policy identity and donor-facing lane.
candidates.vulnerability: Rubio competes for the same networks; intervention backlash limits expansion.
candidates.positions: Hawkish foreign policy and tariff skepticism distinguish his pitch.
candidates.money: Historical presidential donors do not establish present commitments.

candidates.path: A speculative opening built on nationalist personnel and withdrawal experience.
candidates.coalition: A potential audience; an electoral coalition is not established.
candidates.advantage: Substantive personnel authority and actual withdrawal work.
candidates.vulnerability: No demonstrated presidential organization or current faction commitments.
candidates.positions: Historical restrictionist staffing and withdrawal advocacy; current specifics need review.
candidates.money: Thiel’s dating-business investment is not a nomination endorsement.

cross_implications.title: A negotiating role is also a succession asset.
cross_implications.assessment: Vance’s war postmortem offers differentiation from hawkish rivals while his earlier public defenses retain exposure. That is strategic positioning, not a measured transfer of primary support.

cross_implications.title: New gatekeeping changes the channels contenders must navigate.
cross_implications.assessment: Miller’s announced promotion could broaden his agenda access. It supplies no evidence that he or the White House has chosen a nominee.

relationships.assessment: Different post-election war arguments supply competing succession pitches. No measured support transfer is established.
The announced chief-of-staff transition changes prospective access. The handover and allocation of political responsibilities remain to be verified.
Historical backing supplies a channel into the nomination coalition. It does not establish agreement on every policy or a new 2028 pledge.

power_shifts.role_change: Chief of staff → reported political-operation role
power_shifts.implication: Less White House agenda gatekeeping; campaign-resource influence may persist.

power_shifts.role_change: Deputy chief of staff → announced chief of staff
power_shifts.implication: A broader agenda and staffing channel for enforcement hardliners; this does not itself change policy.

power_method.title: Role-based agenda access · 0–5
power_method.scale: 0 no identified channel; 1 outside access; 2 political-operation channel; 3 deputy-level White House role; 4 chief-of-staff gatekeeping; 5 presidential decision authority.
power_method.status: Conditional post-handover scenario, not an observed transfer or a calibrated measure of total faction power. Scores are ordinal analyst judgments, not percentages.
power_method.condition: The reported November 9 handover and political-operation remit must occur as described.
power_method.policy_projection: Greater hardliner access could prioritize enforcement and staffing. It does not guarantee Iran escalation: the ledger also records Miller’s reported exit pitch. Democratic oversight and funding pressure may constrain both camps.
